hypotheses.justification: 𝒪 is an argument because the statement mentions it, so this instance-implicit variable is pulled in. The statement only needs `CommRing 𝒪`, since `opFamily M H S 𝒪` needs `CommRing 𝒪` and `NeZero M` and nothing else. The proof uses `diamondL_top_eq_one`, whose signature takes only `(𝒪 : Type) [CommRing 𝒪]`. It also uses `CohCarrier.heckeT_comm_of_prime`, whose hypotheses are `NeZero ℓ`, `NeZero ℓ'`, primality, coprimality and `AddCommGroup V`; here V = 𝒪, which gets `AddCommGroup` from `CommRing`. The domain property is never used, so the theorem holds and the same proof works after deleting it, for example with `omit [IsDomain 𝒪] in`. It can be deleted independently of the other two.
